principles: Learn useful chunks before isolated rules
Pronunciation and listening are trained together
Grammar is learned as meaning and viewpoint, not formulas only
Every lesson ends with spoken output
Review is spaced and connected to real situations

languageLabs.title: Grammar as Meaning
languageLabs.description: Tenses, articles, modals and sentence patterns explained through the mental picture they create — not just formulas.

languageLabs.title: Sound System
languageLabs.description: IPA, stress, rhythm, reductions, linking and intonation — the layer that makes fast English become audible.

languageLabs.title: Native Pragmatics
languageLabs.description: How English speakers soften, imply, disagree, react and manage social distance in real conversation.

languageLabs.title: Language Deep Dive
languageLabs.description: Understand English as a system: word order, information flow, stress timing, register, collocation and language change.

phases.title: Rebuild the Foundation
phases.description: Stop translating word-by-word. Rebuild core grammar, high-frequency chunks, sound awareness and everyday reaction patterns.

phases.title: Train the Ear & Mouth
phases.description: Connected speech, stress, rhythm, phrasal verbs and conversational situations until English starts to feel physically natural.

phases.title: Think & Interact in English
phases.description: Handle requests, opinions, stories, disagreement, travel, work and advanced grammar without falling back to translation.

phases.title: Own the Language
phases.description: Build register, nuance, long-form speaking, fast-listening tolerance, professional English and a durable English identity.

Countability and how English packages things

Sentence stress: hear the important words

Reductions: gonna, wanna, kinda & real speech
Schwa /ə/: the most useful English sound
R, L, TH and final consonants
Give opinions with confidence and nuance
Agree and disagree without sounding harsh
Storytelling: make events easy to follow
Everyday wellbeing & talking about how you feel
Cultural pragmatics: what people really mean
Passive voice: control focus and responsibility
Gerunds & infinitives: action as thing or direction
Emphasis: clefts, do, really and contrast
Stance: signal certainty, attitude and evidence
Coherence: make your English easy to follow
Paraphrasing when the exact word disappears
Long turns: speak for 2–3 minutes smoothly
Decode fast speech without chasing every word
Podcasts, videos & learning from authentic input
Networking: start, sustain and exit conversations
Debate: challenge ideas without attacking people
Fluency checkpoint: own your second language
